anchor: The virus infects the host cell.
paraphrase: The host cell is infected by the virus.
edit: The host cell infects the virus.
notes: The edit is biologically absurd, so world knowledge alone could separate it.

critique.reason: A cell infecting a virus is biologically absurd, so world knowledge settles it. The asymmetry is the sentence's whole content, so no swap is plausible. The paraphrase is also a bare passive.

anchor: The tide pushed the boat toward the rocks.
paraphrase: The boat was driven toward the rocks by the tide.
edit: The rocks pushed the boat toward the tide.
notes: The edit is physically odd, so world knowledge alone could separate it.

critique.reason: Rocks pushing a boat is physically absurd, and this is not a clean swap: goal and agent trade places while the patient stays. Any repair is a different sentence.

paraphrase: The sun is circled by the earth.
notes: The edit is false as a fact, so world knowledge alone could separate it.

critique.reason: 'The sun orbits the earth' is a textbook false statement, so world knowledge alone decides it. The fact is the content, so it can't be repaired.

anchor: Some of the data was lost in the outage.
paraphrase: The outage wiped out part of the data.
edit: All of the data was lost in the outage.

critique.reason: 'All' entails 'some', so it has the same flaw as quant-08. The only repair ('only some') makes it a copy of the fixed quant-08.

anchor: The vast majority of farmers here grow wheat.
paraphrase: Growing wheat is what nearly all farmers here do.
edit: A tiny minority of farmers here grow wheat.

critique.reason: 'Vast majority' to 'tiny minority' is a stock antonym pair of fixed phrases, so it tests antonyms too. It repeats quant-02 (most to few), and the available repairs copy quant-02 or quant-07.

anchor: Sound travels about 340 meters per second in air.
paraphrase: In air, sound covers roughly 340 meters each second.
edit: Sound travels about 3,400 meters per second in air.

critique.reason: 340 m/s is a textbook constant, so 3,400 is false on world knowledge alone. Any other number has the same problem. It also repeats the times-ten pattern.

notes: The paraphrase assumes a diagnostic test.

critique.reason: 'Detected the condition' imports a medical context, and 'positive' has no neutral synonym to repair it with. 'Came back negative' is also a stock phrase.

anchor: Not every bird in the aviary can fly.
paraphrase: Some birds in the aviary are unable to fly.
edit: No bird in the aviary can fly.

critique.reason: 'No bird can fly' entails 'not every bird can fly', so only the implicature separates them: the some/all flaw. It also tests quantifiers. Every placement of the negation over 'every' has this entailment, so it can't be repaired.

anchor: The doctor advised him not to drive.
paraphrase: The doctor's advice was that he should avoid driving.
edit: The doctor did not advise him to drive.

critique.reason: 'Advise' is a neg-raising verb: 'did not advise him to drive' is commonly heard as 'advised him not to drive', so the edit doesn't clearly differ. Changing the verb copies scope-04 or scope-08.

anchor: They did not plan to close the factory.
paraphrase: Closing the factory was not part of their plan.
edit: They planned not to close the factory.

critique.reason: 'Plan' is neg-raising: 'did not plan to close' and 'planned not to close' are near-synonyms in ordinary use, so the edit doesn't clearly change the meaning.

anchor: We chose not to renew the lease.
paraphrase: We decided to let the lease run out.
edit: We did not choose to renew the lease.

critique.reason: 'Choose' is neg-raising: 'did not choose to renew' is routinely heard as 'chose not to renew'. The difference is too weak for a clear test.

anchor: Not all of the cookies contain nuts.
paraphrase: Some of the cookies are nut-free.
edit: None of the cookies contain nuts.

critique.reason: Same entailment as scope-01 ('none' entails 'not all'), and a one-word quantifier swap, so it tests quantifiers. Same shape as scope-01.

anchor: It is not true that all the files were deleted.
paraphrase: Some of the files survived the deletion.
edit: It is true that none of the files were deleted.

critique.reason: 'None deleted' entails 'not all deleted', the same implicature-only flaw as scope-01. 'Survived the deletion' also adds an event, and the shape repeats scope-01 at clause level.

anchor: Only the nurses can open the cabinet.
paraphrase: The cabinet opens for nurses and nobody else.
edit: The nurses can only open the cabinet.

critique.reason: second read: same move as scope-26, and the edit was ambiguous

anchor: Mina never forgets to lock the gate.
paraphrase: Locking the gate is something Mina always remembers.
edit: Mina always forgets to lock the gate.

critique.reason: second read: never to always is a frequency swap with no scope change; repeats quantifier rows

anchor: Visitors must not leave without signing out.
paraphrase: Signing out is required of visitors before leaving.
edit: Visitors need not sign out before they leave.

critique.reason: second read: repeats scope-11, and the edit rewrote the sentence
